BNY.thesis_one_line: World's largest custody bank compounding fee income faster than the market's implied growth, but already re-rated sharply so upside is more modest now.
kill_criteria: Noninterest (fee) income growth YoY falls below 3% for two consecutive quarters (current run-rate +11%, not ~19%: DV06 2026-10-08)
Net interest income declines >15% YoY for two consecutive quarters without an offsetting fee acceleration (NII is currently +20% YoY: DV06 2026-10-08)
CET1 ratio falls below 10.5% (management's medium-term target is about 11%; ratio is 11.0% at 30 Jun 2026) forcing a buyback pause
Diluted EPS misses consensus (FY0 $9.26 / FY1 $10.26) by >5% for two consecutive quarters
A material operational/cyber incident affecting custody settlement is disclosed in an 8-K
key_adverse_facts: Fee income is the larger driver of recent revenue growth (fee and other revenue +11% YoY, 427 of the 670 Q2 revenue increase) but net interest income is also rising (+20% YoY, 1,446 vs 1,203) [Corrected 2026-10-08 by DV06: the earlier '-10%' was gross interest income]; earnings remain market-level dependent
Stock already up ~51% over the trailing year per Q04 triage, so street consensus upside is only ~11.5% from here
CET1 11.0% at 30 Jun 2026 (11.9% at Dec-25) against a medium-term target of about 11%; YTD payout 87% (FY25 94%) [Corrected 2026-10-08 by DV06: CET1 now sourced from the 2Q26 release]
data_conflicts: Q4-2025 gap closed by DV06 (2026-10-08): 4Q25 release shows revenue 5,179, EPS 2.02; dossier revenue column was gross interest plus noninterest income, not reported revenue
Guidance language corrected by DV06 (2026-10-08): primary-source 2026 outlook (Ex-99.3) is revenue up 10-11% and expenses up 6-7% (Jul 2026 update), not an NII range
BNY.confidence_in_thesis: medium - strong franchise and valuation math support inclusion, but CET1/AUC-A data gaps and reliance on market-linked fee growth warrant a smaller position and follow-up

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for BNY. Restated by DV06 (2026-10-08): bank P/TBV-ROTCE test (P/TBV 4.58x; required sustainable ROTCE 32.4% at cost of equity 9.43%, 3% terminal growth, vs ROTCE 31.3% in Q2'26 and a 33%+ medium-term target) is in line; payout-basis reverse DCF implies 5.0-6.0%/yr versus base 8-9% (original 4.1% treated 100% of net income as distributable at a 4.2% risk-free rate). Verdict unchanged.

BNY.scenario_basis: Starting FY0 consensus EPS $9.26, NTM P/E ~15.0x; bear = 3%/yr EPS growth + multiple compression to 12x; base = 9%/yr EPS growth + flat 15x multiple; bull = 13%/yr EPS growth + re-rating to 17x; all cases add ~1.4-1.5%/yr dividend yield, annualized over 3 years.

CL.thesis_one_line: Global #1 in toothpaste with unmatched emerging-market reach, priced for less margin recovery than management is likely to deliver, but growth is modest and momentum is negative.
kill_criteria: Operating margin (GAAP) stays below 20% for three consecutive quarters
Organic/constant-currency revenue growth falls below 2% for two consecutive quarters
Diluted GAAP EPS declines YoY for two consecutive quarters
Dividend payout ratio (on GAAP EPS) exceeds 100% for two consecutive quarters
key_adverse_facts: Operating margin in the last two reported quarters (18.1%, 19.0%) is below the year-ago comparable quarters (21.9%, 21.1%) while gross margin rose 140bp; DV09: the fall is Strategic Growth and Productivity Program charges ($129m in Q2, $300m in H1) plus advertising +15%, not tariff or COGS inflation (Base Business EPS +8%); Q4-25 was a 1.8% operating margin and a net loss, so GAAP operating margin has been below 20% for three consecutive quarters and GAAP EPS down YoY for three consecutive quarters (kill criteria 1 and 4 already met as written)

Consolidated stockholders' equity is structurally near zero ($54m-$856m range over the last two years, from decades of buybacks) - not a solvency risk but a real disclosure item limiting balance-sheet flexibility
12-month price momentum is -13.7%, the weakest of the three F101 names
DV09: total debt fell to $7,857m at 30 Jun 2026 from $8,758m a year earlier (net debt $6,404m vs $7,346m); the earlier 'rose from $7.0bn to $7.8bn' compared two different XBRL concepts
data_conflicts: Trailing P/E of 33.9x (GAAP) vs NTM P/E of 21.3x reflects one-off charges depressing trailing EPS; the adjusted reconciliation was not independently rebuilt this session
DV09 verified guidance in the Q2-26 8-K Ex-99: FY26 net sales +2% to +6%, organic +1% to +4%, GAAP EPS double-digit growth, Base Business EPS mid-single-digit growth (raised)
Q4-2024 and Q4-2025 (Oct-Dec) quarterly figures were gaps in this session's XBRL pull; DV09 derived Q4-25: revenue $5,230m, operating income $92m (1.8% margin), net loss $(37)m, EPS $(0.04)
CL.confidence_in_thesis: low-medium after DV09: verdict moved INCLUDE-SMALL -> WATCH because GAAP kill criteria 1 and 4 are already met (driven by disclosed restructuring charges); re-base the criteria on Base Business measures and read Q3-26 (30 Oct 2026) before re-including

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: No V1 row exists for CL; own reverse DCF (7.5% WACC, 3% terminal growth) implies ~2.3%/yr 10-year FCF growth versus a base case of ~6-7%/yr, so the market is pricing in materially less growth than a plausible base case.

CL.scenario_basis: Starting FY0 consensus EPS $3.88, NTM P/E ~21.3x; bear = 2%/yr EPS growth + multiple compression to 18x; base = 7%/yr EPS growth + flat 21x multiple; bull = 10%/yr EPS growth + re-rating to 24x; all cases add ~2.5%/yr dividend yield, annualized over 3 years.

EMR.thesis_one_line: Diversified process-automation and software franchise (with AspenTech) growing steadily, but the price already reflects close to a reasonable base case and a known GAAP-vs-adjusted gap is unresolved.
kill_criteria: Organic revenue growth (per the 10-Q's own non-GAAP reconciliation) falls below 3% for two consecutive quarters
The trailing/NTM P/E gap widens further without an explicit one-off/restructuring disclosure
FY2026 guidance (given at Q4 FY2026 earnings, ~Nov 2026) is cut from the consensus-implied run-rate (FY1 EPS $7.26)
key_adverse_facts: Trailing P/E (34.2x) is ~1.6x NTM P/E (21.8x), consistent with the Q09 triage's own red flag; this session confirms the gap exists but does not resolve whether it is one-off or structural
Quarterly GAAP net income is volatile quarter-to-quarter (e.g., $329m to $996m within FY2024), consistent with unreconciled restructuring/AspenTech consolidation noise
The b1 quant composite (0.326, decile 4) is the weakest of the three F101 names - this is a triage-judgment pick, not a strong factor signal
Analyst target range is unusually wide ($104-$205), signalling real disagreement on AspenTech-adjusted earnings power
data_conflicts: DV15: total debt at 30 Jun 2026 is $13,113m (short-term $5,587m + long-term $7,526m), not the $8.92bn 10-K LongTermDebt figure; TTM FCF is $3,462m, not $3.706bn
Company FY2026 adjusted EPS guidance ~$6.55 (raised Aug 4 2026); $7.26 is NTM consensus
EMR.confidence_in_thesis: medium-low - reasonable business but the valuation gap vs base case is too thin, and the GAAP/adjusted noise flagged at triage is confirmed but not resolved

valuation_view_vs_v1.reconciliation: DV15 restated: own reverse DCF at WACC 9.9% (UST 5.17% + 1.23 x 4.5% ERP) on TTM FCF after SBC (~$3.22bn) implies ~11.7-13%/yr 10-year growth versus base 8-9%: priced above the base case.

EMR.scenario_basis: Starting FY0 consensus EPS $6.56, NTM P/E ~21.8x; bear = 2%/yr EPS growth + multiple compression to 17x; base = 9%/yr EPS growth + flat 21x multiple; bull = 14%/yr EPS growth + re-rating to 24x; all cases add ~1.4%/yr dividend yield, annualized over 3 years.
